analysis: Both changed files are test-only, so no shipped provider code or runtime behavior changes. (1) EngineV2PrefillGeometryTests.swift (added, 383 lines) tests EngineV2Factory.prefillGeometry and productionSchedulerConfig: Gemma 4 takes a wide 2048 chunk, other families keep the SDK geometry, and env overrides (chunk, step budget, stripe) roll back or opt in. The tests check that paged-pool ring sizing max(chunk, stripe) is unchanged, that bidirectional media keeps a narrower chunk ceiling, and that malformed or nonpositive values fall back to the SDK. They also check that an undersized Gemma chunk override is raised to gemma4MaximumMediaBlockTokens so media blocks cannot trip the PagedSequenceKV ring precondition, which is availability-relevant. The engine tests use DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0, KVBackendGuardStore path /dev/null and stub tokenizers. They touch no real keys, network or on-disk cache artifacts, and introduce no secrets. (2) EngineV2ProductionWiringTests.swift line 312 only extends a switch to cover the new .toolCallDelta event case (ignored via continue). That is a test-helper compile adaptation with no security effect. The production geometry change (not in this batch) affects prefill chunking, which touches T-010 and T-029 availability and the T-041 prefix cache only indirectly. Prefix cache is disabled in the tests, and no change to cache scope, TTL, HMAC naming or the encryption posture is visible. Integration question for production code review: confirm that the wide chunk plus step budget at 8x32k concurrency does not cause GPU memory exhaustion (DoS) beyond the Gemma floor. This cannot be confirmed from test code alone, and the tests themselves note activation peaks rose for other families. Also confirm that toolCallDelta handling in production does not leak partial tool-call content outside the encrypted path (T-008). No findings.
